text: Black Condor is the superhero name used by three distinct fictional characters in the DC Comics universe, all of whom have been members of the Freedom Fighters and have appeared in Freedom Fighters comic books published by DC Comics. The first Black Condor, Richard Grey Jr., was created by Quality Comics writer Will Eisner (under the pseudonym Kenneth Lewis) and artist Lou Fine, and first appeared in Crack Comics #1 (cover-dated May 1940), continuing through issue #31 (October 1943), and also appearing in Uncle Sam Quarterly #2 (December 1941). As an infant, Richard survived an archaeological expedition in Outer Mongolia when his family was killed by bandits led by Gali Kan; he was rescued and raised by a condor who taught him to fly by studying the movement of wings, body motions, air currents, balance, and levitation. A mountain hermit named Father Pierre eventually discovered and civilized the child, teaching him to speak English. Richard later tracked down and killed the bandits and traveled to the United States, where he uncovered a plot to assassinate Senator Thomas Wright, though he was too late to save him. He then adopted the identity of Black Condor to fight corrupt politicians, rum-runners, and racketeers. His strip was popular and became Crack Comics' featured story starting in issue #3, with Lou Fine drawing the first 24 stories and the feature running through issue #31. According to Kurt Mitchell in American Comic Book Chronicles: 1940–1944, the character's flight scenes, with their dynamic perspectives and graceful motion, were unmatched by Superman's portrayal. Jess Nevins' Encyclopedia of Golden Age Superheroes notes that Richard fought femmes fatale, the Eagle Battalion, Yellow Perils, Kite-Men (Japanese agents on flying kites), a Chinese mad scientist, a golem, and killer robots known as the Spinning Deaths. In the DC Universe, his powers were retconned to stem from exposure to a radioactive meteor. He joined Uncle Sam and the Freedom Fighters and later the All-Star Squadron, and participated in the JLA: Year One miniseries as part of a group of Golden and Silver Age heroes who helped repel an Appellaxian invasion. He also appeared as an ethereal "spirit guide" in Ryan Kendall's Black Condor series. The second Black Condor, Ryan Kendall, gained flight, telekinesis, and healing powers through genetic manipulation by his grandfather, Creighton, who was part of the Society of the Golden Wing attempting to create a flying human. Kendall was the only success of these experiments and eventually rebelled, escaping Creighton, who repeatedly tried to recapture him. Ryan initially believed he was not a superhero but later fought alongside other heroes, including Primal Force and Justice League International, and settled in Opal City. He sought insight from Hawkman and assisted in battles, such as against Karen Ramis, the post-Zero Hour Lion-Mane. In Infinite Crisis #1, he was killed by Sinestro, later resurrected as a Black Lantern in Blackest Night and permanently resurrected in Dark Nights: Death Metal. The third Black Condor, John Trujillo, is of Mayan descent and received his powers from the Mayan Spider Goddess Tocotl. He sees himself as a protector of the universe and first appears when he rescues Uncle Sam and the Freedom Fighters from agents of S.H.A.D.E. He is serious and uncomfortable with social interactions, rebuffing a romantic overture from the Phantom Lady, which she later realizes was not genuine. The full extent of his powers is unrevealed, but he can fly at extremely high speeds, control the wind, and may possess moderate superhuman strength and speed. The Richard Grey Jr. incarnation of Black Condor also appears in the Batman: The Brave and the Bold episode "Cry Freedom Fighters!", voiced by Jason Charles Miller.
